lead: 3x Nasdaq 100 ETF / TQQQ — the dip-buy meets 7.5% inflation
smaller: 20+Y Treasury ETF / TLT — the safe haven that sank with stocks
Walt Disney / DIS — the beat that survived inflation day
Uber Technologies / UBER — the beat the market sold anyway
why_lead: The 10 February US CPI (known at this cutoff) is the dominant catalyst: CNBC 7.5%, highest since 1982 [[n2132]], Reuters 'largest annual gain in 40 years' [[n1196]], 10-year above 2% [[n2192]], 'big-bang' March hike case [[n2201]]. TQQQ is the retail vehicle that expresses buy-the-dip faith with leverage and shows the reaction most sharply (58.82 USD, -6.63% in one session, -22.95% over 20 versus Nasdaq 100 -7.54%), and there is genuine crowd-attention evidence: Financial News London on Reddit's meme-stock investors turning to the bearish 'dark side' [[n1833]], Seeking Alpha's retail-facing QLD-versus-TQQQ leverage piece [[n1808]], NBC News on investors whose 2021 gains evaporated [[n1810]] and The Economist on the GameStop saga [[n0380]]; the analog rests on Reuters' commentary that a central bank drain questions 'buy the dip' [[n1361]] and the 1970s comparison Ideastream rebuts [[n1351]]. Relation to earlier retail notes: the strictly earlier 2022-02-04 draft ran TQQQ only as a secondary 'leveraged dip-buy snaps back' item; this lead is a material update built entirely on newly published 10 February CPI and Fed-speaker evidence ([[n2132]], [[n2192]], [[n2201]], [[n1363]], [[n1833]]). The 2022-02-04 item's daily-reset decay angle is not repeated: the 20-session TQQQ (-22.95%) versus Nasdaq 100 (-7.54%) figures appear only as a price fact, and the triggers are the 2-year yield, the Fed's first move and the VIX.
why_smaller: 20+Y Treasury ETF / TLT ('the safe haven that sank with stocks'; hook changed from 'bond bunker' to avoid echoing the 2022-02-10 Coca-Cola 'dividend bunker'): the failed-safe-haven narrative (bonds and stocks falling together) — TLT -1.59% to 136.23 USD as the S&P 500 fell 1.81%, 10-year above 2% [[n2192]], PBS on the Fed [[n2204]], Fortune's peak-inflation counter-case [[n2131]], bear flattening on the card; not used in any strictly earlier retail note or draft (2022-02-01 to 2022-02-10); the only adjacent theme is the 2022-02-10 Coca-Cola item's Reuters line on investors switching out of bonds into dividend funds.

Walt Disney / DIS: deliberate brief carryover of the 2022-02-10 lead with a material update — the completed 10 February session (+3.35% to 152.16 USD on a down day, +8.66% over five sessions) and newly published 10 February evidence (TechCrunch 11.8M new subscribers [[n1171]], Reuters 'closes gap with Netflix' [[n0803]]); kept secondary and under 160 words; its break uses a Disney-specific trigger (Netflix 406.27 USD, -24.38% over 20 sessions; the 157.80 USD level) rather than repeating the lead's 2-year-yield caution.

Uber Technologies / UBER: the sell-the-beat narrative — -6.07% to 37.75 USD after Reuters' 2024 profit forecast shortfall [[n0864]] and WSJ's 'hungry for more' [[n0865]], despite the Guardian's profitability headline [[n0866]]. In the 2022-02-10 edition Uber appeared only as supporting reopening evidence inside the Disney lead; this is its first item, with a new (negative) reaction.
considered_not_chosen: Affirm / AFRM (-21.42%, the biggest single-session drop) and DoorDash / DASH (-9.54%): no own-date headline explaining the moves.
Zillow (GeekWire 'shares up 16%' [[n0881]]) and Twitter ($4 billion buyback [[n0861]]): no card price rows.

Coca-Cola / KO results beat ([[n0798]], [[n0799]]): KO was the 2022-02-10 secondary item; the results are not used in this edition (the Social Signal now rests on retail-attention headlines rather than a corporate results headline).
Bitcoin / BTC-USD (-1.74%) and Ether (-5.00%) after CPI: crypto ran on 2022-02-04, 02-07, 02-08 and 02-09; no new crypto-specific catalyst beyond the macro print.

Avoided as misdated: CNBC 'Dow slides 500 points as yields spike following red-hot inflation report' ([[n0686]]) is stamped 9 February but describes 10 February trading (content precedes this cutoff, but the stamp is misdated, so it is not cited); Reuters LIVE MARKETS pages ([[n0826]], [[n1326]]) were rejected as rolling live blogs.
